Ascent

uh-SENT -- a homophone of 'assent' (agreement); ascent is about climbing, assent is about agreeing. This unit teaches only the climbing sense. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Ascent is an instance of climbing or moving upward; a way up.

The hikers paused halfway through their steep ascent to catch their breath.

Worked Example

A mountaineering team spends eight hours climbing steadily upward along an icy ridge, gaining thousands of feet in elevation before finally reaching a resting point near the summit.

That steady climb upward, gaining height step by step, is exactly what an ascent is. It is entirely unrelated to 'assent,' which means agreement -- the two words are pronounced alike but mean completely different things.

How Ascent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

climb

climb: an act of moving upward, often with effort

rise

rise: an upward movement

ascension

ascension: the act of rising or climbing to a higher position

Antonyms

descent

descent: a movement downward

decline

decline: a downward slope or movement

How Strong Is It? — rise → ascent → climb

rise vs. ascent

rise vs. ascent: Rise is a more general word than ascent -- rise can describe anything moving upward, even smoke or prices, while ascent specifically describes a physical climb, often a strenuous one.

climb vs. ascent

climb vs. ascent: Climb can feel more effortful than ascent in casual speech, though the two are close in meaning: ascent is the more formal, often technical term used for mountaineering and aviation.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a- (ad-)

prefix — a- (ad-): toward (Latin)

root — -scend-

root — -scend-: to climb (Latin (scandere))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin scandere meant 'to climb.' Ascent, at its root, means a climb toward something -- literally 'a climbing to.' Its opposite, descent, uses the same root with de- ('down') instead.

Use the root in a new word: descend

Use the root in a new word: descend: The plane began to descend rapidly as it approached the runway.

Word Choice

Ascent describes a climb, whether up a mountain, a staircase, or figuratively up a career ladder -- never to be confused with its homophone 'assent,' meaning agreement.
